text:
Sampled HR@10 measures performance against the specified 99 negatives; it does not establish full-catalog HR@10. Sampled metrics can reverse model rankings relative to exact metrics ([Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). Repeatedly optimizing a small validation set also creates selection optimism, potentially comparable to differences between algorithms ([Cawley and Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)). Preserve the pinned evaluator and describe conclusions as conditional on its users, candidates, and seeds.

Suggested uncertainty analysis: retain each model’s per-user binary hit outcomes; bootstrap paired user indices independently within each category, preserving model pairing, then average the four category means equally. Report the macro difference’s 95% interval and category differences. This follows the paired-resampling principle documented by [SciPy](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html). With 200 users/category, one changed hit moves category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. These intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on fixed candidates and training seed; they neither measure training variability nor correct adaptive selection bias. Holm adjustment suits a prespecified family of valid comparisons, but does not rescue unrestricted adaptive validation reuse ([Holm](https://www.ime.usp.br/~abe/lista/pdf4R8xPVzCnX.pdf)).

Suggested budget plan: predeclare a compact search space, comparison count, checkpoint schedule, and minimum worthwhile gain. Use staged resource allocation inspired by [Hyperband](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v18/16-558.html), retaining all four datasets and required seeds. Charge every concurrent trial, diagnostic, and failure against 43,200 GPU-seconds; reserve compute for full-budget finalists and component-removal ablations. Select by the required macro HR@10, report uncertainty descriptively, and leave held-out evaluation untouched.
